topic: Lido v4 source-execution oracle and uint256 arithmetic correction, 2026-09-28

facts.value: getPooledEthByShares requires sharesAmount < UINT128_MAX then uses a plain uint256 product under Solidity 0.4.24. The product wraps before division; balanceOf delegates to that function.
facts.note: Compiled unchanged function bodies independently reproduce the accepted-input counterexample: N=2^128, M=N-1, total M, external 0, buffered/deposited M each, holder M-1. Source returns N-6 while previous unbounded Rust returned 2N-4. No deployed reachability claim.

facts.value: Internal ether sums four packed uint128 fields using SafeMath.add. External ether multiplies externalShares by internalEther unchecked, then divides; total pooled ether adds with SafeMath. The individual packed-width bounds do not imply an aggregate uint128 bound.
facts.note: Two further compiled-source counterexamples prove wrapping even when the mathematical final quotient fits uint256, and MATH_ADD_OVERFLOW after a valid external product. Mapper spec 4 matches those outcomes, omitting only the failed derived total and preserving all six stored inputs. Host references remain outside production WASM.

facts.value: The local solc 0.4.24+commit.e67f0147 macOS amd64 binary matches official SHA256 7034c4048bc713d5c14cdd6681953c736e2adbdb9174f8bfbfb6a097109ffaaa.

open_questions: Current deployment code hashes, dependency/epoch activation, actual reachability of extreme packed states, initialized checkpoints and actual package/getter controls remain unverified.
The conservative unsupported externalShares > totalShares domain and missing-holder Unknown remain explicit host guards, not claims of Solidity revert equivalence.
